patients.label: 3-year-old girl with a subglottic foreign body that migrated to the left main bronchus after tracheostomy and bronchoscopy

identity_evidence.quote: A 3-year-old female presented with two days history of cough and difficulty in breathing.

attribution_limitations: The first rigid bronchoscopy is described incompatibly: the PAHS paragraph (b00005) says the FB was not visualised upon advancing the bronchoscope into the trachea, while the next paragraph (b00006) says the FB was located above the tube level and became dislodged during attempted extraction; the abstract says it migrated during the first attempt. The procedure is kept once as performed (p1-f022) and the two findings are quarantined as source_conflict facts.
The cause of the FB migration is the authors’ hypothesis (manipulation, uncuffed tube, thin FB), not a documented finding.

The discussion says rigid bronchoscopy was tried 'even after identification of FB location after imaging (CT scan)', which could place a CT before the first rigid attempt or refer to the second rigid bronchoscopy; the case text calls the CT post-operative, after the abandoned first procedure. The discussion also calls the FB a suspected bone while the case reports a retrieved bone chip.
The route is stated as "Intravenous antibiotics and steroids"; the route is recorded for antibiotics only and not borrowed for steroids.

She was initially admitted in pediatric ward with a diagnosis of croup and treated with oxygen and steroids. Lack of symptomatic improvement on the following day raised suspicion of FB.
Then, the patient was referred to Patan Academy of Health Sciences (PAHS) with an uncuffed tracheostomy tube.

At PAHS, rigid bronchoscopy was attempted; however, the FB was not visualised upon advancing the bronchoscope into the trachea. Flexible bronchoscopy through the tracheostomy tube also failed to locate the FB up to the primary bronchus. Due to the child’s unstable condition, the tracheostomy tube was left in place, and the procedure was abandoned. A post-operative CT scan revealed the FB had migrated to the left main bronchus (Figure 2).

An initial rigid bronchoscopy was performed without removing the tracheostomy tube, as the foreign body (FB) was located above its level. During attempted extraction, the FB became dislodged. Subsequent flexible bronchoscopy through the tracheostomy tube failed to visualize the FB up to the primary bronchi, and the procedure was aborted due to hemodynamic instability. A second rigid bronchoscopy was performed 8 to 10 hours later following removal of the tracheostomy tube.
